cefrAlignment: Fits B1 (CEFR CV reading for information: can find and understand relevant information in everyday material such as brochures and short official documents): a course brochure and short profiles of about 210 words each, with tasks focused on names, numbers, times and simple synonyms.
examFidelity: The gap task uses the authentic IELTS wording 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER' and every key fits the limit; the TOEFL Read in Daily Life and TOEIC Part 7 tips agree with exams.ts.
fixes: Removed the 'All of them' option from ex2 q1 (an all-of-the-above-style distractor)
Added reasonable accepted answers to the gap for the minimum age ('8 years', 'eight years', '8 years old') and a hyphenated phone-number variant
Changed Sofia's 'kitchen team of fifteen people' to 'fifteen volunteers' so the ex3 item 'leads a group of other volunteers' has one clearly defensible answer
learnerOutcome: A learner can predict the form of an answer, scan a short everyday text quickly for names, numbers, dates and prices, and check that a detail belongs to the right person or event even when the question uses synonyms.
